clue.text: Miserly type, cold fish, saving pile

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe within, so the cold-and-fish pair holds the pile inside it

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a skate is a flat fish
a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: A stingy person is described as a cold fish who hoards a pile of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is someone who hates spending, which is exactly what this slang word for a stingy person describes.

clue.text: Caught? Then long time in prison

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A criminal is arrested and then serves a long sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a barred enclosure for confining someone serves as a place of imprisonment.

clue.text: Part of the time residents upset recluse

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top
part of means only some letters of the phrase are taken, inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Some locals are sometimes annoyed by a hermit in their midst.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ETIMERE sits across 'the time residents' and 'upset' turns it the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hermit who withdraws from society, especially for religious reasons.

clue.text: One who takes after writer, New York tightwad

indicators.note: after places the taker word following the writer and the city

parts.note: a pen is something that writes
a pincher is one who pinches or takes, i.e. steals

explanation.surface: A thief who follows a New York author is a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a skinflint who counts every coin is a stingy person, as is a tightwad.

clue.text: An afterthought squeezed into gift bag

indicators.note: squeezed into means pressed inside, so the afterthought sits within the gift word

parts.note: a knack is a gift or talent
PS, postscript, is an afterthought at the end of a letter
an is the indefinite article, A

explanation.surface: A late addition crammed into a present bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a backpack carried on the shoulders is a kind of bag.

clue.text: Ditch swimmer crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the swimmer word straddles the river letter

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish, so a swimmer

explanation.surface: A swimmer abandons the attempt to cross a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a verb meaning abandon, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a long narrow dug channel, as in wartime trenches.

clue.text: Fashionably smart young woman docked

indicators.note: docked means having the tail cut off, so the last letter of the word for a young woman goes

parts.note: chick is slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A stylish young woman whose boat has come into port.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something stylish and elegant in a modish way is described with this French-derived adjective.

clue.text: Abandoned in vestibule, something a traveller may carry

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the abandoned word goes inside the vestibule word

parts.note: a hall is an entrance vestibule
old in the sense of former, given up or no longer in use

explanation.surface: A traveller's luggage left lying in the entrance lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large soft bag for carrying clothes and belongings on a journey.

clue.text: There's much talk from me about supposedly mad character on strike

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for circa, about
the Hatter in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland is famously mad
to box is to strike with the fist

explanation.surface: A gossip notes the many rumours about an eccentric figure who has downed tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a person who talks incessantly would say this about themselves, the clue speaking in their voice.

clue.text: Prepare gen vigorously for consultation document

indicators.note: doing something vigorously suggests energetic stirring, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to put together background information energetically ahead of a policy consultation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gen' is British slang for information, which makes the surface plausible. In British politics this is the government's preliminary discussion paper on proposed policy.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK government, a preliminary paper setting out proposals for public discussion before legislation is known by this name.

clue.text: Excuse made by Tuck, endlessly?

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter, so the last letter of the fold word is dropped

parts.note: a tuck is a fold sewn into fabric, i.e. a pleat

explanation.surface: Friar Tuck offering some excuse that goes on without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an excuse put forward in one's defence is an appeal or pleading of this kind.

clue.text: German writer enclosing long frightening story

indicators.note: enclosing means surrounding, so the German writer wraps round the long word

parts.note: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and dramatist
to pine is to long or yearn

explanation.surface: A German author producing an extended horror tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thriller or horror story that sends a shiver down one's back.

clue.text: Very small container attached to back of lorry

parts.note: a tin is a metal container

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here taken from lorry

explanation.surface: A little container hitched to the rear of a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something minute or very little is described with this everyday adjective.

clue.text: Crawler, extremely smarmy chap, not refined

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters
refined here means processed and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grovelling man who is very oily and lacks polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not refined' looks like a description of the chap, but 'refined' is the anagram signal and 'not' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawler is a toady who flatters superiors to gain favour, and this word names such a fawning flatterer.

clue.text: Antagonism in place after work

indicators.note: after places the place word following the work abbreviation

parts.note: OP, opus, is a musical work
a position is a place

explanation.surface: Hostility that sets in once a job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: resistance or hostility towards someone or something is antagonism.

clue.text: Prince unhappy with court and shopping centre

indicators.note: unhappy suggests being put out of sorts, so the letters of the royal word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A miserable prince arrives at a mall with his courtiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrianised shopping area in a British town is often called by this name, also used for a police district.

clue.text: Wrath involving large one catching fish?

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the word for wrath wraps around the letter for large

parts.note: anger is wrath
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Fury taking hold of a big fellow who is trying to land a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a person who fishes with rod and line is one who catches fish.

clue.text: Decline drink and go

parts.note: to down is to drink quickly
a turn is a go, as in 'your turn'

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a drink and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb meaning refuse, but it is a noun meaning a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fall or slump in economic activity is a decline.

clue.text: Duty of force in charge close to palace

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here from palace

explanation.surface: The obligations of the officer commanding the police near the royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a duty or function someone is charged with, as in the office of mayor.

clue.text: Suitability of female, one giving evidence after wife dismissed

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the wife letter is removed

parts.note: a witness gives evidence in court

explanation.surface: A court questions whether a woman testifying is fit, after her spouse was thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being appropriate or apt for a purpose is suitability.

clue.text: Study awful rot written about church music

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn

indicators.note: awful suggests something botched, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Reading some dreadful nonsense penned about the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a noun but is the old verb meaning learn; the church abbreviation joins the rot in the scramble that 'awful' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a composition for solo instrument and orchestra is one form of music.

clue.text: Get back on track in France, impressed by meandering course

indicators.note: impressed by means pressed into, so the France letter sits inside the shuffled letters
meandering means wandering, so the letters of course are rearranged

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A river's winding route in France gets back to its original line.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to concentrate again on the proper aim is to get back on track.

clue.text: Highly delighted? Not true

definitions.meaning: very pleased, as in British slang for thrilled

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to hear something that turns out false.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this phrase for thrilled, and it also means invented or fictitious.

clue.text: At sea, chiefly?

definitions.meaning: the main is an old poetic term for the open ocean, so being on it means being afloat
mostly or for the most part

explanation.surface: A sailor's question about being mainly on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means 'mostly', and read literally places one on the ocean, an archaic sense of 'main'.

clue.text: Dubious fines collected by city on a regular basis

indicators.note: collected by means gathered inside, so the regular letters enclose the fines
taking letters on a regular basis means every other one, here the second and fourth of city

parts.note: F stands for fine (as on pencil leads), so two fines give two Fs

explanation.surface: Questionable penalties gathered by a city council at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: something doubtful or of uncertain quality is described with this colloquial adjective.

clue.text: Clerical dignitary blowing top immediately

indicators.note: blowing one's top means losing it, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A senior churchman losing his temper at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic synonym: 'soon, presently, at once', as in Shakespeare's 'I come anon'.

clue.text: Piece of information I came across on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means travelling in reverse, so the met word is read backwards

parts.note: met means came across, encountered

explanation.surface: Someone recounts a bit of news picked up while returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a single detail or news report, as in a news piece.

clue.text: Politician managed to entertain European known to all

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the managed word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
public knowledge is known to everyone

explanation.surface: An MP who organised hospitality for a famous continental guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of the US party opposed to the Democrats, or an opponent of monarchy, is a kind of politician.

clue.text: Set of tables in fine study?

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the phrase fine study, across the word break

explanation.surface: Some furniture placed in an elegant private room.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of small tables of graded sizes that slot under one another is called by this name.

clue.text: Love quiet reformed person in penal establishment

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: reformed means reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tender, peaceful rehabilitated offender within the prison system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link to the definition but is part of the anagram fodder with 'person'.
explanation.definitionFit: A minimum-security jail where inmates have more freedom is a type of penal establishment.
